help_tip_git_diff: Staged changes & commit: use the Diff tab in the workbench to stage files and create commits.
help_tip_git_stash: Save work in progress: in the Diff tab → Stash, push a stash to keep changes without committing.
help_tip_mentions: Use @ to mention a file directly in the chat and give the agent explicit context.
help_tip_no_git: Initialize a git repo: open the Diff tab in the workbench to enable version control.
help_tip_no_workspace: Add a folder: click the workspace selector in the chat footer to start working with files.
help_tip_plan_mode: Plan mode: the agent pauses and shows the full plan before running any destructive tool, one approval instead of one per tool.
help_tip_rag_search: Search memory directly: use the search field in the Memory tab to query RAG without waiting for the agent to cite it.
help_tip_shared_terminal: The agent's terminal is the same one you see in the panel — long-running commands stream live on both sides.
help_tip_slash_commands: Type / in the chat to see available commands (e.g. /model to switch models).
help_tip_subagents: Delegate tasks: ask the agent to delegate to a subagent (coder/search) — the run history shows up in the Tasks tab.

onboarding_api_keys_body: Configure keys for the AI model and search tools (all have a free tier). You can skip and add them later in Admin → Settings.
onboarding_api_keys_google_desc: Main model — code, reasoning and chat.
onboarding_api_keys_ollama_hint: Prefer 100% local, no cloud keys? Skip this step and set up Ollama afterwards in Settings → Environment → Gateways — it covers the model and embeddings, and web search falls back automatically without a key.
onboarding_api_keys_tavily_desc: Real-time web search for the agent.
onboarding_backup_body: Choose the data categories to restore from your backup.
onboarding_capabilities_bullet_browser: Browser: dev server preview and free navigation of external sites.
onboarding_capabilities_bullet_files: Files and terminal, with optional sandboxing per workspace (Sandbox).
onboarding_capabilities_bullet_git: Full git — commit, branch, amend, squash, cherry-pick and more.
onboarding_capabilities_bullet_library: Library: install MCP connectors, skills and memory buckets.
onboarding_capabilities_bullet_schedule: Schedule recurring tasks or a one-off subagent run in the background.
onboarding_capabilities_intro: Whatever you can do in this app by hand, the agent can do too — and vice versa.
onboarding_done_body: You're all set — start a conversation and Vectora will get to work!
onboarding_memory_conversation_body: Every agent already remembers everything said in the current conversation — no setup needed.
onboarding_memory_intro: Vectora keeps context in three layers, each working differently.
onboarding_memory_rag_body: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) vectorizes your documents and past conversations so Vectora can search and follow your existing patterns and docs, without retraining the model.
onboarding_memory_remember_body: Every few turns, Vectora proposes reusable skills or facts it noticed — always with your approval, visible afterwards in the Plan tab.
onboarding_mode_body: Choose how Vectora stores its data. "Lite" uses local SQLite + LanceDB, with an embedded NATS covering queues and pub/sub, and works out of the box. "Complete" uses PostgreSQL + Qdrant + Redis — exclusive to the Pro plan, for anyone who already has self-hosted or third-party services (Supabase, Upstash, Qdrant Cloud, etc).
onboarding_mode_complete_desc: PostgreSQL + Qdrant + Redis — exclusive to the Pro plan; requires connection setup.
onboarding_mode_lite_desc: SQLite + LanceDB + NATS — local, with built-in queues and pub/sub, ready to use.
onboarding_mode_self_hosted: Self-hosted (allow Vectora to start this service)
onboarding_mode_start_command_placeholde: Start command (e.g. docker compose up -d postgres)
onboarding_mode_validation_warning: Test the connection for PostgreSQL, Redis and Qdrant successfully before continuing.
onboarding_pre_mode_body: Choose where Vectora will run — this changes how it identifies you.
onboarding_pre_mode_local_desc: Local use, no account — free forever.
onboarding_pre_setup_error: Couldn't set up local mode. Please try again.
onboarding_pre_vps_body: Running Vectora on a server is a premium feature — you need a VECTORA_TOKEN with a Pro plan to unlock it.
onboarding_pre_vps_token_invalid: Invalid token, or not a Pro plan.
onboarding_token_body: Are you a Pro user? Connect your account with your Vectora Token and unlock your features.
onboarding_token_free_note: On the Free plan? You can link your account too, but it's optional — nothing changes for you. You can skip this and add the token later in Admin → System.
onboarding_token_login_copy_hint: Copy the token and paste it in the field above.
onboarding_token_login_hint: Sign in to your vectora.company account and copy your token from the dashboard.
onboarding_welcome_body: Vectora is your AI coding assistant — it can read, write and run code inside your trusted folders.
onboarding_workspace_body: Workspaces are folders on your machine that Vectora can access when you grant trust.
onboarding_workspace_bullet_1: Add a folder in the Workspace selector in the chat composer.
onboarding_workspace_bullet_2: Vectora can read and write files only inside trusted folders.
onboarding_workspace_bullet_sandbox: Terminal and file access can be sandboxed per workspace via a [sandbox] section in vectora.toml — auto-enabled when a usable WSL2 distro is detected, otherwise off until you configure it.
permission_desc_plan: Propose only — never run destructive tools
plugins_subtitle: Connect external MCP servers; their tools become available in chat.
preferencias_dialog_desc: Manage your account, preferences and memory.

prefs_fonts_godot_help: Inter and JetBrains Mono are the default fonts used by Godot 4. The selected families must be installed on your system.
prefs_image_fallback_help: When the active model can't process images and the message has an attachment, use this model automatically instead of blocking the send.
prefs_media_models_hint: Ollama and OpenRouter only — Gemini and OpenAI resolve on their own. An empty field falls back to the environment variable, if set.
prefs_mono_font_help: Font used by terminals, diffs, and code blocks.

prefs_timezone_hint: Used by schedules: "every Monday at 9am" means 9am in this zone.

prefs_training_placeholder: E.g.: When writing SQL, always use lowercase keywords.
prefs_ui_font_help: Font used by the rest of Vectora.
prefs_ui_scale_help: Adjusts the size of everything — text, icons, and spacing — at once.
prefs_weekly_insight_help: Shows aggregated technical metrics only, without conversation content.

provider_routing_openrouter_subtitle: Proxy with hundreds of models via a single API key. Get yours at openrouter.ai/keys.

stack_go_1: Run go vet and fix any issues
stack_go_2: Identify any goroutine leaks or race conditions
stack_go_3: Improve error handling across the codebase
stack_java_1: Run static analysis and fix critical findings
stack_java_2: Add unit tests for the core business logic
stack_nodejs_1: Review package.json dependencies and suggest upgrades
stack_nodejs_2: Find performance bottlenecks in the Node.js code
stack_nodejs_3: Add TypeScript types to the main entry points
stack_python_1: Run the tests and fix any failures
stack_python_2: Check for unused imports and dead code
stack_python_3: Add type hints to the main functions
stack_rust_1: Run cargo clippy and fix the warnings
stack_rust_2: Add documentation comments to public items
stack_rust_3: Look for opportunities to reduce heap allocations
stack_unknown_1: Explain the project structure and key files
stack_unknown_2: Find and fix any bugs or issues in the codebase
stack_unknown_3: Write tests for the most critical functions
